chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl narrated from Amr ibn Uthman, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Zurarah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) accepted the jizyah from the People of the Covenant on the condition that they do not consume usury, do not eat the meat of pigs, and do not marry sisters, nor the daughters of brothers, nor the daughters of sisters. Whoever among them does that, the covenant of Allah and the covenant of His Messenger is free from him.
He said: Therefore, they do not have a covenant today.
And that which indicates that once she has completed her waiting period, she becomes permanently forbidden to him is what has been narrated.
ai.seo_question: What were the conditions for accepting jizyah from Ahl al-Dhimmah according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the theological basis for the *dhimma* (covenant) by linking the validity of the poll tax to specific behavioral prohibitions, notably usury, pork consumption, and consanguineous marriage. In Shia jurisprudence, this serves as a foundational text for understanding how the revocation of these conditions—either through non-compliance or the passage of time—nullifies the covenant, thereby affecting the legal status of non-Muslims under Islamic rule. The reference to the *iddah* period underscores the permanence of certain marital prohibitions, reinforcing the structural integrity of the covenant's terms.
